summary: Contrast methane and water while distinguishing atoms from electron-pair guides.
objective: Compare methane and water in 3D and let me show electron-pair guides separately from atoms.
example_prompts: Compare methane and water in 3D and let me show electron-pair guides separately from atoms.
Rotate water to see why a tetrahedral electron-pair arrangement does not mean four bonded atoms.

claims.statement: Methane has tetrahedral molecular geometry. Water has tetrahedral electron-pair geometry but bent molecular geometry, with a bond angle about 104.5 degrees.
claims.scope: Introductory idealized VSEPR comparison of CH4 and H2O; no quantitative electronic-structure claim.

claims.statement: The ideal electron-pair geometries have fixed angles: linear 180 degrees, trigonal planar 120 degrees, tetrahedral 109.5 degrees, trigonal bipyramidal 90 and 120 degrees, and octahedral 90 or 180 degrees. Methane has a tetrahedral arrangement of its hydrogen atoms and, having no lone pairs, a molecular structure identical to its electron-pair geometry, whereas the greater space taken by lone pairs reduces the water bond angle to 104.5 degrees, below the ideal tetrahedral value.
claims.scope: Ideal VSEPR angles and the lone-pair reduction that separates water's molecular geometry from its electron-pair geometry. No bond lengths, atomic radii or energies are claimed.

source_refs.locator: 7.6 Molecular Structure and Polarity, electron-pair geometry table and the water discussion: tetrahedral "all angles 109.5 degrees"; linear 180, trigonal planar 120, trigonal bipyramidal 90 and 120, octahedral 90 or 180; methane with "a tetrahedral arrangement of the hydrogen atoms" where "the molecular structure is identical to the electron pair geometry"; for water "the bond angle is 104.5 deg", smaller than the ideal tetrahedral angle because lone pairs occupy more space than bonding pairs

defaults.rationale: Both angles are printed in the cited section and carried by claim.molecular-shape-comparison and claim.molecular-shape-ideal-angles; the coordinates below are the exact placements that realise those sourced angles at unit bond length, so a build can be checked against arccos values rather than by eye. Bond length is deliberately absent: the section gives angles only, and the record already warns that display radii are not measured properties, so lengths stay a display unit chosen by the scene. Tunable in bond length and display radius; the two angles are not tunable, because they are the content the recipe exists to show.

water_hydrogen_directions.note: each at half of 104.5 deg from the +y symmetry axis: sin(52.25 deg) = 0.79016, cos(52.25 deg) = 0.61292

equations: angle(H-X-H) = arccos(u1 . u2) for unit bond direction vectors
tetrahedral: u_i . u_j = -1/3 for every pair, giving arccos(-1/3) = 109.4712 deg
a rigid camera transform leaves every dot product unchanged

worked_example.inputs: Methane with the four hydrogens along (+-1,+-1,+-1)/sqrt(3) with an even number of minus signs, and water with two hydrogens at +-52.25 degrees from the +y axis in the xy plane, both at unit bond length
worked_example.expected: Every methane H-C-H angle measures 109.4712 degrees, matching the sourced ideal 109.5 to within 0.03 degrees; the water H-O-H angle measures exactly 104.5 degrees; both readings are unchanged by any camera orbit, and toggling the lone-pair guides changes neither the atom count (5 for methane, 3 for water) nor either angle
worked_example.derivation: Methane: u1 . u2 = (1 x 1 + 1 x -1 + 1 x -1)/3 = -1/3, so the angle is arccos(-1/3) = 109.4712 deg; the same holds for all six pairs by symmetry. Water: u1 . u2 = -0.79016^2 + 0.61292^2 + 0 = -0.62435 + 0.37567 = -0.24868, and arccos(-0.24868) = 104.4 deg; using the exact half-angle 52.25 deg gives cos(104.5 deg) = -0.25038 and the angle back to 104.5 deg, so the coordinates should be stored to at least five decimals or derived from the angle at load time. Camera check: dot products are invariant under rotation, so the measured angle cannot change with the view - if it does, the measurement is being taken in screen space.

tolerance.angle_deg: +/- 0.1 deg on a measured angle against its sourced value; the 109.4712 exact value differs from the section's rounded 109.5 by 0.03 deg, which is a rounding difference, not an error
tolerance.atom_count: exact: guide visibility must never change it
tolerance.camera_invariance: the measured angle must be identical to 1e-9 deg before and after any camera move
